# Konstrukt

> The Hooman Loop design system (v2.0.0). Swiss / Bauhaus: `--radius: 0px`, `--shadow: none`, one palette (`atelier`), light and dark via `data-mode` on `<html>`. Tokens are authored as W3C DTCG JSON and generated into CSS, Swift/SwiftUI, `dist/tokens.json`, and a text/ASCII layer.

This file is generated by `node build/llms-full.mjs` from the documents listed below. Do not edit it by hand. After changing any of those sources, run `npm run build:llms` and commit the result.

Included: AGENTS.md, DESIGN.md, README.md, docs/text.md, CONTRIBUTING.md.

---

source: AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md

Instructions for coding agents working in or consuming Konstrukt. The full
contract is [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) — read it before changing tokens, gates, or
outputs. This file is the short path in, not a second spec.

## What this is

Konstrukt is The Hooman Loop's public, MIT-licensed design system. Tokens are
authored once as W3C DTCG JSON and generated into CSS, Swift/SwiftUI, a
resolved JSON manifest, and a text/ASCII layer. Version 2.0.0 ships one
palette, `atelier`, in light and dark.

## Hard rules

- Square corners. `--radius: 0px`. Do not introduce border-radius.
- No shadows. `--shadow: none`. Elevation is borders and weight, never blur.
- Use tokens. Never hard-code hex values, radii, or shadows in consumer CSS,
  Swift, or docs. A token path is the CSS custom property:
  `status.draft-bg` → `--status-draft-bg`.
- One palette: `atelier`. Light and dark are selected with
  `data-mode="light"` or `data-mode="dark"` on `<html>`.
- `data-palette` is accepted and ignored. 1.x names (`hl`, `sqdl`, `courage`,
  `minimal`, `blueprint`) are aliases that render as atelier; they go away in
  3.0. `[data-theme="dark"]` still aliases `data-mode="dark"`.
- Contrast is gated. 80 foreground/background pairs must meet WCAG 2.2 AA
  (4.5:1 text, 3:1 controls) in both modes.

## Where things live

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `tokens/` | Author here — primitives, global, semantic, dark, deprecated, text |
| `src/` | `base.css`, `theme.js`, `text.css`, text renderer and linter |
| `build/` | Generator plus parity, contrast, and llms-full gates |
| `dist/` | Generated. Never hand-edit. Gitignored. |
| `docs/` | In-repo static docs (`npm run docs`). Public page: https://thehoomanloop.com/konstrukt/ |
| `proposals/` | Unstable. No version, no gate, no compatibility promise. |

Consumers never read `tokens/` directly. They consume `dist/`.

## Build and check

```bash
npm install
npm run build       # tokens/ → dist/{css,swift,tokens.json,text.json,text.py} + docs/assets
npm run check       # parity vs build/canonical-tokens.css + WCAG AA contrast
npm run check:text  # text-layer linter + golden board
npm run check:llms  # llms-full.txt matches sources; llms.txt links resolve
npm run snapshot    # accept an intended token change (commit the snapshot with it)
npm run docs        # http://localhost:4340
```

If you edit `DESIGN.md`, `README.md`, `docs/text.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, or
this file, run `npm run build:llms` and commit the regenerated `llms-full.txt`.

A new output needs a gate. A new primitive needs a real consumer in the same
pull request. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Consuming tokens

| Surface | How |
|---------|-----|
| Vanilla HTML | `dist/css/konstrukt.css` + `base.css` + `theme.js` |
| Astro / Vite / React | `@import '@hooman-loop/konstrukt/css'` |
| iOS / SwiftUI | Add `dist/swift/Konstrukt`; read `@Environment(\.konstruktTheme)` |
| Tooling / AI | `dist/tokens.json` — `themes["atelier.light"]`, `themes["atelier.dark"]`, plus `text` |
| Text / CLI | Vendor `dist/text.py`, or read `dist/text.json` for raw ladders |

The live public docs page is https://thehoomanloop.com/konstrukt/. It is built
from a different repo and may lag this one. After `npm run build`, read
`dist/tokens.json` locally.

## When to use the text layer

Use it for chat, CLI, SMS, logs, and other character-cell channels — not for
pixel UI. Nine primitives (`spark`, `hbar`, `grid`, `range`, `multi`,
`annotate`, `kv`, `frame`, `ruler`) live in `src/text/renderer.py` and ship as
`dist/text.py`. Glyph ladders and column budgets are tokens
(`tokens/text.json`). The spec is [docs/text.md](docs/text.md). Run
`npm run check:text` after changing any of that.

## Agent entry points

- [llms.txt](llms.txt) — curated index (the build also copies it into `docs/`)
- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) — generated full docs
- [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) — the contract

source: DESIGN.md

# Konstrukt — design system contract

Konstrukt is the single source of truth for design tokens across the Hooman
Loop ecosystem. Tokens are authored once as JSON and generated into CSS,
Swift/SwiftUI, a machine-readable JSON manifest, and a text/ASCII output
layer. Every surface — the portal, the marketing site, internal tools, native
iOS, and character-cell channels — consumes the same generated values.

## Aesthetic

Bauhaus / Swiss International Typographic Style: flat surfaces (`--shadow: none`),
square corners (`--radius: 0px`), Space Grotesk for display, Inter for body,
SF Mono for code. Authority through typography and a restrained palette, not
chrome.

## One palette, two modes

Konstrukt 2.0 ships one palette, `atelier`, in two modes set on `<html>`:

| Attribute | Values |
|-----------|--------|
| `data-mode` | `light` (the `:root` default) · `dark` |
| `data-palette` | accepted and ignored |

The 1.x palettes (`hl`, `sqdl`, `courage`, `minimal`, `blueprint`) were cut in
2.0.0. `theme.js` and the Swift package normalize those names to `atelier`, so
stored preferences and old call sites keep rendering. `[data-theme="dark"]`
still aliases `data-mode="dark"`.

## Token layers

| Layer | File | Emitted? | Referenced as |
|-------|------|----------|---------------|
| Primitives | `tokens/primitives.json` | no | `{color.teal.700}`, resolved at build time |
| Global | `tokens/global.json` | yes | fonts, type scale and roles, spacing, strokes, radius |
| Semantic | `tokens/semantic.json` | yes | light-mode roles; may link to each other with `var(--x)` |
| Dark | `tokens/themes/dark.json` | yes | overrides only the roles that differ |
| Deprecated | `tokens/deprecated.json` | yes | 1.x names as `var()` aliases, removed in 3.0.0 |

Semantic roles: surfaces (`bg`, `bg-alt`, `surface`), type (`text`,
`text-muted`), structure (`ink`, `border`, `border-light`), accent (`accent`,
`accent-soft`, `accent-light`, `on-accent`, `focus`), feedback (`success`,
`warning`, `danger`, `info`, each with `-bg`), `status-*` (which link to the
feedback roles), `category-1` to `category-5`, and selection.

Konstrukt does not know product vocabulary. Segments, invoice states and
timelines are mapped onto `category-*` and feedback roles in the product's own
stylesheet.

## Source of truth

```
├── tokens/                      # AUTHOR HERE — W3C DTCG JSON
│   ├── primitives.json          # raw color ramps, referenced, never emitted
│   ├── global.json              # fonts, type scale + roles, spacing, strokes, radius
│   ├── semantic.json            # :root light roles (surfaces, text, accent, feedback…)
│   ├── deprecated.json          # 1.x aliases, removed in 3.0.0
│   ├── text.json                # glyph ladders, column budgets, reserved marks
│   └── themes/dark.json         # dark-mode overrides
├── build/                       # generator + parity / contrast / text gates
├── src/                         # base.css, theme.js, text.css, text renderer + linter
└── dist/                        # GENERATED — never hand-edit
    ├── css/konstrukt.css        # :root (light) + dark selector blocks
    ├── css/base.css             # portable components (.module, .badge, …)
    ├── css/theme.js             # HLTheme runtime
    ├── css/text.css             # pre.kt embed styles
    ├── swift/Konstrukt/         # Swift package
    ├── tokens.json              # resolved manifest, one entry per theme, plus text
    ├── text.json                # resolved text-layer spec
    └── text.py                  # self-contained Python renderer
```

Token naming maps directly to CSS custom properties: a token at path
`status.draft-bg` becomes `--status-draft-bg`. Edit JSON, then run the build.

## Build & verify

```bash
npm install        # first time
npm run build      # tokens/ -> dist/{css,swift,tokens.json,text.json,text.py} + docs/assets
npm run check      # parity vs build/canonical-tokens.css + WCAG AA contrast
npm run snapshot   # rebuild and accept the output as the new snapshot
npm run check:text # text-layer linter + golden board
npm run check:llms # llms-full.txt freshness + llms.txt link check
npm run build:llms # regenerate llms-full.txt from the contract docs
npm run docs       # serve docs on http://localhost:4340
```

From the monorepo root:

```bash
make konstrukt-build   # build + parity check
make konstrukt-docs    # build + serve docs
make sync-tokens       # build + distribute CSS to every consumer
```

### Parity gate

`build/canonical-tokens.css` is the committed snapshot of the generated CSS.
`npm run check:parity` confirms the build still matches it value-for-value
(selector by selector, declaration by declaration). A failure is either a
generator regression or an intended token change. For the latter, run
`npm run snapshot` and commit the snapshot diff with the token change, so the
reviewer sees exactly which custom properties moved.

Through 1.x the snapshot was the original hand-authored portal `tokens.css`.
It was regenerated in 2.0.0, when the token model changed.

### Contrast gate

`npm run check:contrast` checks every foreground/background pair the
components render, in both modes, against WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for
control outlines, focus rings and structural rules. The pairs are listed in
`build/check-contrast.mjs`. A new role that renders text needs a row there.

## Consuming Konstrukt

| Surface type | How to consume |
|--------------|----------------|
| Vanilla HTML | `<link rel="stylesheet" href=".../konstrukt.css">` + `base.css` + `<script src=".../theme.js">` |
| Astro / Vite / React | `@import '@hooman-loop/konstrukt/css';` or the synced `konstrukt.css` |
| iOS / SwiftUI | Add the `dist/swift/Konstrukt` package; read `@Environment(\.konstruktTheme)` (see `docs/ios.html`) |
| Tooling / AI | Read `dist/tokens.json` (resolved per theme, plus `text`) |
| Text / CLI | Vendor `dist/text.py`, or read `dist/text.json` for raw ladders |

`make sync-tokens` copies `dist/css/konstrukt.css` into each web consumer and,
for the portal, also `base.css` and `theme.js`. The portal's
`portal/css/tokens.css` is now a generated artifact — edit tokens here, not
there.

## Adoption status

Konstrukt is consumed at three levels of trust. The distinction matters because
only the first kind is verifiable from this repo.

| Surface kind | Tokens | Notes |
|---------|--------|-------|
| Marketing site (Astro) | generated | `src/styles/konstrukt.css` refreshed from `dist/` by a sync step. |
| Product portal | generated | `tokens.css`, `base.css`, `theme.js` synced from `dist/`. |
| Client sites | imported | their stylesheet imports the synced `konstrukt.css`. |
| Internal dashboards | synced | token file synced, but a runtime stylesheet may still inline a token subset. |
| Internal agent lanes | bridged | imports the synced `konstrukt.css` while keeping a legacy `--color-*` vocabulary. |
| Native iOS | generated | SwiftUI package built from `dist/swift/`. |

Legacy `--color-*` token names are deprecated in favor of the canonical names
above. Surfaces still on the old vocabulary keep working via their own `:root`
blocks until migrated.

source: README.md

# Konstrukt

[![verify](https://github.com/the-hooman-loop/konstrukt/actions/workflows/verify.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/the-hooman-loop/konstrukt/actions/workflows/verify.yml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-067F8A?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)

The Hooman Loop design system. JSON-first design tokens, generated into CSS,
Swift/SwiftUI, a JSON manifest, and a text/ASCII output layer, with a
self-contained documentation site.

Konstrukt is the single source of truth: edit tokens in `tokens/`, run the
build, and every surface — web apps, marketing sites, internal tools, native
iOS, and character-cell channels — follows.

![Konstrukt landing page](assets/readme/hero.png)

One palette · light + dark · 43 color roles · 8 type roles · 4 output
targets · WCAG AA gated · 0px radius · 0 shadows. Bauhaus / Swiss
International: flat surfaces, square corners, authority through typography
rather than chrome.

## One palette, two modes

Konstrukt ships a single palette, **atelier**: warm off-white, near-black ink,
one teal accent. `data-mode="light" | "dark"` on `<html>` switches between two
flat token sets resolved at build time. No runtime theme math in the browser.

Tokens are layered: raw color ramps in `tokens/primitives.json` are referenced
as `{color.teal.700}` and resolved at build time, never emitted. Semantic roles
(`accent`, `danger`, `status-review`, `category-3`) are what consumers use, and
dark mode overrides only the roles that differ.

![The components page in light and dark mode, side by side](assets/readme/modes.png)

## Quick start

```bash
npm install
npm run build      # tokens/ -> dist/ (CSS, Swift, tokens.json, text) + docs/assets
npm run check      # parity vs the committed snapshot + WCAG AA contrast
npm run snapshot   # accept an intended token change
npm run check:text # text-layer linter + golden board
npm run docs       # serve the docs site on http://localhost:4340
```

## What it produces

| Output | Path | For |
|--------|------|-----|
| Themed CSS | `dist/css/konstrukt.css` | all web surfaces (light + dark) |
| Components | `dist/css/base.css` | portable Konstrukt components |
| Theme runtime | `dist/css/theme.js` | `HLTheme` — sets the mode on `<html>` |
| Text embed | `dist/css/text.css` | `pre.kt` styling for character-cell blocks |
| Swift package | `dist/swift/Konstrukt/` | iOS / SwiftUI |
| Manifest | `dist/tokens.json` | tooling, design apps, AI agents (includes `text`) |
| Text spec | `dist/text.json` | glyph ladders, column budgets, reserved marks |
| Text renderer | `dist/text.py` | vendored into cron collectors, briefings, CLI tools |
| Docs site | `docs/` | reference + integration guides |

## Tokens

Every token is authored once, in W3C DTCG JSON, and its path becomes its CSS
custom property: `status.draft-bg` → `--status-draft-bg`. The reference page
reads the generated manifest, so what you see is what ships.

<img src="assets/readme/tokens.png" width="820" alt="Token reference: surfaces and text, accent and borders, feedback, status, categories">

Typography is tokenized too. Each role (`display`, `heading`, `subheading`,
`label`, `badge`, `body`, `meta`, `mono`) is emitted as a `font` shorthand
plus tracking and case, and the Swift package gets the same roles as
`KonstruktTextStyle`:

```css
h1 {
  font: var(--type-display);
  letter-spacing: var(--type-display-tracking);
}
```

Border widths are tokens as well: `--stroke-hairline` (1px), `--stroke-rule`
(the 2px ink rule) and `--stroke-rail` (the 4px accent rail).

<img src="assets/readme/typography.png" width="820" alt="Typography reference: font families, eight type roles rendered live, and the type scale">

## Contrast

Every foreground/background pair the components render is checked against
WCAG 2.2 AA in both modes: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for control outlines, focus
rings and structural rules. `npm run check` fails the build when a pair drops
below. 80 pairs pass today.

## Components

The portable component vocabulary: modules with 2px ink borders, status pills,
category tags, primary and quiet buttons, form fields, alerts, data tables,
question lists. Square by default, no shadows, teal reserved for the one
primary action on a surface.

<img src="assets/readme/components.png" width="820" alt="Component reference: modules, badges, category tags, buttons, form fields, alerts, data table, cards, progress">

## Text layer

Charts, annotations and CLI motion for channels that render characters instead
of pixels. Nine primitives, two encodings, and a linter that fails a build when
a chart lies about a number.

The text layer is part of the versioned contract. Glyph ladders, column budgets
and reserved marks live in [`tokens/text.json`](tokens/text.json). `npm run build`
emits `dist/text.json` and a self-contained `dist/text.py` for vendoring. Read
the spec: [`docs/text.md`](docs/text.md). Run the renderer:
`python3 dist/text.py`.

<img src="assets/readme/text-layer.png" width="900" alt="Konstrukt text layer one-pager">

example data; the phones are mockups, not device captures.

## Documentation

- Design system reference and live token explorer: `npm run docs`, or the

  [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) (working in this repo). The live public docs page is
  [thehoomanloop.com/konstrukt](https://thehoomanloop.com/konstrukt/).

## Editing tokens

Author tokens in `tokens/` as W3C DTCG JSON. A token's path becomes its CSS
custom property (`status.draft-bg` → `--status-draft-bg`). Never edit anything
in `dist/` — it is generated. After editing, run
`npm run build && npm run check && npm run check:text`. If the parity gate
fails because you meant to change a value, run `npm run snapshot` and commit
the snapshot diff alongside the token change.

## Proposals

`proposals/` holds work that is under review and promises nothing. It has no
version, no gate, and no compatibility guarantee. When a proposal is stable it
is promoted into `tokens/` and `src/` through the checklist in
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md), and only then does it ship.

## Contributing

Read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) first. The short version: a new
output needs a gate, a new primitive needs a real consumer in the same pull
request, and a vendored copy carries a version stamp.

## License

MIT for the code and tokens. The Konstrukt name and marks are not covered by
the license. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).

source: docs/text.md

# Konstrukt · Text — spec

Status: shipped in 1.2.0. Part of the versioned contract.

Artifacts:
- `tokens/text.json` — glyph ladders, column budgets, cell counts, reserved marks
- `src/text/renderer.py` — reference renderer (source)
- `src/text/lint.py` — conformance linter, `--self-test` proves 11 of 11 checks
- `dist/text.json` — resolved spec, emitted by `npm run build`
- `dist/text.py` — self-contained renderer for vendoring, baked from the tokens
- `dist/css/text.css` — `pre.kt` embed styles for a Konstrukt page
- `dist/tokens.json` — includes a top-level `text` block
- `scripts/text_board_page.py` — builds the review sheet as a Konstrukt HTML page

## 1. The gap

Konstrukt is a *rendered surface* system. Its colour tokens are pixels: colour,
spacing, radius, fonts. Every artifact that leaves the pixel world used to
invent its own grammar.

- Briefing scripts held `SPARK_GLYPHS = "▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█"`, a hand-rolled
  `sparkline()`, and a 16-point compass spelled out as a tuple.
- The eight-column contract that makes that chart readable lived in a `wanted`
  set in the collector, not in the primitive. Hand the same primitive fifteen
  hourly points and it renders 54 columns and nothing complains.
- CLI status output, progress and spinners were written inline wherever needed.
- The prompt that consumed it carried a paragraph of prose explaining how to
  read the chart, because the chart had no spec to point at.

That is one working renderer. The drift risk is the second one: a new agent
writes a 7-level ladder, or `#` bars beside `█` bars, or carets under the wrong
column, and nothing catches it because there is no token, no reference, no test.

Text is not a smaller web surface. It has one resolution axis, a fixed cell, and
a channel that may refuse colour. What transfers is not pixels, it is the
authority structure: hard edges, mono metadata, one accent, status words.

## 2. The translation table

This is the design argument. Everything else follows from it.

| Konstrukt (pixels) | Konstrukt · Text (cells) |
|---|---|
| `--radius: 0` | square corners only: `┌ ┐ └ ┘`, never `╭ ╮` |
| `--border` 2px ink | heavy box drawing `┏ ┓ ┗ ┛ ━ ┃` for a block frame |
| `--border-light` | single `┌ ─ │` for rules inside a block |
| `.module-head` (1fr auto) | first line: `LABEL` left, meta right-aligned to budget |
| `.micro-label` mono uppercase | `LABEL` uppercase, two spaces, no colon |
| `.row` (1fr auto) | label padded, value right-aligned, numerics right-justified |
| `.pill` | `[NORMAL]` `[WATCH]` `[VET]` |
| `.progress-fill` | fixed 8-cell ladder `████░░░░` |
| `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` | automatic: the cell grid is tabular |
| `--accent` teal | ANSI / HTML colour where the channel has it, never alone |
| `--text-muted` | lowercase, or `·` separators |
| `.status-strip` | `──` rule plus one KPI line |
| `.page-header` | `┏━` frame, kicker uppercase, status pill right |

Two things do **not** transfer and must be replaced, not scaled:

- **Type scale.** There is no 12/14/18/32 in a chat message. Hierarchy is
  carried by case, position and the frame, and by nothing else.
- **Weight.** Bold is unreliable across channels: it survives Markdown, not
  plain text, not a pasted log. Never encode meaning in weight.

## 3. One new axis: encoding

Konstrukt has palette × mode. The text layer adds a third, orthogonal axis:

| Axis | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `encoding` | `unicode` (default) · `ascii` | same ladder positions, two renderings |

`unicode` uses block and box glyphs. `ascii` maps every position onto
`. : - = + * # @`, `- = # @` and `+ - | =`, for SMS, some email clients, log
files, and terminals with a broken font. Same shape, degraded resolution, never
a different language.

Corollary: **ASCII illustration is out of scope.** Box drawing and block
elements are data glyphs. Cat faces made of slashes are a different craft with
no data contract. The layer owns data marks, not pictures.

## 4. Tokens

Authored in `tokens/text.json`, emitted by `npm run build` as `dist/text.json`
and as the `text` block on `dist/tokens.json`. Consumers never read `tokens/`
directly.

```json
{
  "column": { "phone": 34, "chat": 44, "terminal": 78 },
  "cells": { "spark": 8, "hbar": 8, "range": 16, "multi": 12 },
  "glyph": {
    "unicode": {
      "spark8": "▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█",
      "bar4": "░▒▓█",
      "hbar": { "on": "█", "off": "░" },
      "box-light": { "tl": "┌", "tr": "┐", "bl": "└", "br": "┘", "h": "─", "v": "│" },
      "box-ink":   { "tl": "┏", "tr": "┓", "bl": "┗", "br": "┛", "h": "━", "v": "┃" },
      "mark": { "caret": "▲", "rule": "─", "dot": "·", "dot-on": "●", "pointer": "›" },
      "spin": "▘▝▗▖"
    },
    "ascii": { "...": "same keys, ascii values" }
  },
  "scale": { "percent": { "min": 0, "max": 100 } }
}
```

Glyph ladders are tokens because they are the thing that drifts. A ladder is
a design decision (how many levels before it reads as noise), not a string
literal inside a cron script.

## 5. Nine primitives

Closed set. Anything else is composition. Implemented in `src/text/renderer.py`
and baked into `dist/text.py`.

1. **spark** — one row, N columns, self-normalised curve, with sampling inside
   the primitive so a caller cannot widen it by accident.
2. **hbar** — fixed-scale horizontal bar, 8 or 16 cells, magnitude right-aligned.
3. **grid** — N by M cell matrix on a 4-step ladder, for patterns over time.
4. **range** — a span with the current value marked inside it, for a sleep
   window or a price band where the range matters as much as the point.
5. **multi** — small multiples sharing one scale, so rows are comparable.
6. **annotate** — caret plus label under a specific column of the row above.
7. **kv** — key, dot leaders, value. The text form of `.row-meta`.
8. **frame** — a Konstrukt module in text: heavy frame, head line with meta
   right-aligned, body rows, status pill.
9. **ruler** — a measuring probe, not a chart. See R2.

CLI adds two atoms, which are motion rather than data:

- **spin** — four-frame ladder `▘ ▝ ▗ ▖`, drawn from the same Unicode block as
  the data ladder, so any terminal that can draw a chart can draw the spinner.
  ASCII fallback `| / - \`. Fixed duration per frame, resolved final state.
- **progress** — determinate, 8 cells, count beside it. Never animate a number.

Braille spinners (`⠋⠙⠹⠸`) were the first choice and were rejected: the braille
block is missing from several client fonts and renders as solid tofu, which is
worse than no spinner. Motion borrows glyphs the reader has already proved the
channel can render.

## 6. Rules

R1. **The cell is the pixel.** Align by column index. Never tabs, never
    proportional-font assumptions, pad with spaces, right-justify numerics.

R2. **Width is a contract, and it ships with a measuring device.** Every
    renderer takes a budget from `text.column.<channel>` and truncates with `…`;
    a chart never wraps. Because the real budget depends on the client's font
    and cannot be asserted from a build machine, the system also ships `ruler`:
    paste it into a channel once, and if it comes back ragged, that channel is
    proportional and charts must live inside a code block there.

R3. **Shape is not magnitude.** A self-normalised sparkline must carry its real
    numbers on the same line (`▂▁▃▅▆█▇▅ temp 56→72°`). A bounded domain must pin
    its scale (percent 0-100), so a 9% bar cannot render as a full bar.

R4. **Widen flat ranges.** If the spread is below the minimum, widen it, or a
    two-degree drift renders as mountains.

R5. **One row, one variable.** Two differently scaled series on one line need a
    label per series. Two series sharing a scale share a line, and `multi`
    exists so several rows can share one.

R6. **Absence is signal.** No row when the data is noise. Never a placeholder,
    never an apology for the missing row. A blank cell in a grid is absence, not
    zero, so rows rstrip.

R7. **Colour is never load-bearing.** Every state must be readable in plain
    text. ANSI is a second channel, applied after the shape already says it.

R8. **Emoji are section labels, never data.** `📅 agenda` is fine. Temperature
    encoded as emoji is not.

R9. **Annotate in place.** Caret directly under the column, label under the
    caret, one line, no legend that requires counting. The caret is anchored to
    its column and never moves; the label slides left at the right edge so an
    annotation cannot push a clean block over budget. Derive the caret column
    from the rendered string, because hand-counting is how carets drift.

R10. **Animation resolves.** Every frame ladder ends in a terminal state. No
     animation on numbers. Reduced motion means printing only the resolved frame.

R11. **No mark carries two meanings.** A glyph already spent on one meaning is
     not available for another, because the reader has learned the first one.

     | Mark | Already means |
     |---|---|
     | `↑` `↓` | high / low temperature, or increase / decrease |
     | `▲` | caret: points at the annotated column |
     | `›` | list lead-in |
     | `·` | separator, or idle state |
     | `●` | present / active |
     | `[NORMAL]` | status pill |
     | `▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█` | data ladder: height means magnitude |
     | `▘▝▗▖` | motion only, never a value |

     The live collision is wind: weather widgets spend the arrows on high/low,
     so `↑` next to a wind reading parses as a temperature trend. Wind is
     spelled cardinal (`SSW`), never drawn.

R12. **The ladder is a silhouette, not countable columns.** Adjacent block
     glyphs touch in a monospace font, so an eight-level spark reads as a filled
     profile. That is correct for a trend and wrong for anything where the
     reader must count individual columns. Countable quantities use `hbar` or
     `grid`.

R13. **Eight levels need vertical room.** The same ladder rendered inside a
     13px line box collapses into a silhouette, because the whole scale is being
     drawn in ten pixels of height. Roughly 16px of line box is the floor for
     eight levels. Below that, drop to five levels or use `hbar`, which encodes
     magnitude in width and survives any size.

R14. **A rule without a check is a preference.** Every rule above that can be
     mechanised is mechanised in `src/text/lint.py` and runs in the gate.

## 7. Enforcement

`python3 src/text/lint.py` (or `scripts/text_lint.py`) judges a rendered block
and exits nonzero. Eleven checks:

| Id | Catches |
|---|---|
| T1 | line wider than the column budget |
| T2 | tab characters |
| T3 | trailing whitespace (invisible, poisons golden diffs) |
| T4 | bar ladder and spark ladder mixed in one line |
| T5 | a curve with no number on the line |
| T6 | bar length contradicts the percentage beside it |
| T7 | caret points past its row, or at whitespace |
| T8 | frame lines that do not close |
| T9 | emoji used as a data mark |
| T10 | `↑` `↓` away from a number |
| T11 | two series on one line with no label for either |

`--self-test` lints a block containing one deliberate defect per rule and
asserts 11 of 11 are caught, so the linter itself cannot rot silently.

The point is not tidiness. T6 is a truth check: a bar that says three cells and
a label that says 80% is a chart lying about a number. T5 is the same failure
in the other direction, a shape with nothing to anchor it.

Applied to a live weather chart, honestly:

```
wet day, live path        38 cols   clean
same chart, 15 raw hours  54 cols   T1 over budget
```

The shipped primitive pre-samples to eight points. A caller that bypasses it
and hands raw hourly data still renders 54 columns; the linter catches that as
T1. That is the class of bug the token plus the gate exist to prevent.

`npm run check:text` runs the self-test, lints the reference board in both
encodings, and diffs the board against `build/canonical-text-board.txt`. After
`npm run build` it also requires `dist/text.py` to render byte-identical to the
source renderer.

## 8. Outputs

Consumers are standalone Python scripts and shell tools that cannot take an npm
dependency, so the build emits a vendored runtime plus the raw spec:

| Output | Consumer |
|---|---|
| `dist/text.py` | cron collectors, briefings, mini CLI tools (vendored by copy) |
| `dist/text.json` | anything needing raw ladders without the renderer |
| `dist/tokens.json` `text` block | same spec, next to the colour manifest |
| `dist/css/text.css` | `pre.kt` styling so a text block sits in a Konstrukt page |

Stamp a vendored copy:

```python
# konstrukt-text v1.2.0  sha256:3f9c…  do not edit
```

A copy without a version stamp is indistinguishable from a fork.

Gates:

```
npm run check       # colour parity
npm run check:text  # linter + golden board + generated renderer
python3 src/text/lint.py --file <rendered> --budget 44
```

There is no JavaScript renderer and no Swift text output in this release. The
Python renderer is the supported implementation.

## 9. Still to do

These are follow-ups, not part of 1.2.0:

- A live `docs/text.html` demo page driven from a `dist/text.js` renderer, with
  one section per primitive in the `components.html` anatomy.
- Retrofit of live consumers (morning brief, weekly review, and the rest of
  the table below) so they vendor `dist/text.py` and drop local glyph literals.
- Optional Swift output for terminal tools on the mini.
- Measured column budgets (see open questions).

## 10. Migration targets

Where the grammar pays for itself, in order of reach:

| Surface | Primitives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Morning brief | spark, annotate, frame, kv | the weather chart already ships; it is the first consumer |
| Fitness Sunday programming | hbar, grid, multi | adherence is a pattern over weeks, not a sentence |
| Weekly review | kv, hbar, frame | counts and ratios in aligned columns |
| Usage digest | spark, hbar | model usage is a time series with a ceiling |
| Workday start reminder | kv, pill | agenda and priorities with mono metadata |
| Workspace dashboard | grid, hbar | already Konstrukt in HTML, same grammar in text |
| Job pipeline | kv, hbar | stage counts, not prose |

## 11. Out of scope

- Image charts, and anything needing a rasteriser.
- Markdown tables as a delivery format. Aligned plain text survives a paste
  into a chat; markdown tables do not.
- Emoji as a data encoding.
- Interactive TUI layout, panes, key handling. A framework, not a design system.
- ASCII illustration.

## 12. Open questions

1. Separate package or same package with a second output? Same package, decided:
   it shares the palette, the authority rules and the docs site, and shares none
   of the px tokens. A second repo would drift.
2. Measured column budgets. The numbers in `column` are the shipping defaults.
   Run `ruler` in iPhone Telegram, Slack desktop, Slack iOS and Terminal with
   the same fixture and record what survives. Block glyph advance is the
   specific risk.
3. Keep 8 spark levels or drop to 5? 8 ships and gives resolution, 5 is more
   legible at small sizes. Keep 8 for narrow rows, revisit after the measured
   matrix.
4. Does the palette map to ANSI? If yes, each palette needs a 256-colour value
   plus a documented `--no-color` contract for logs.

## 13. Review sheet

`python3 scripts/text_board_page.py` writes `docs/text-review.html`. Every
string on the sheet comes from the renderer, so the sheet cannot drift from
the grammar it documents.

---

source: CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing to Konstrukt

Konstrukt is a design system with consumers in three languages and at least
four repos. The point of this document is that **adding something is a fixed
sequence, not an act of taste**. Follow it and the system stays honest; skip a
step and a consumer drifts.

## The one rule that decides everything

There are two tiers, and the difference is not maturity, it is **evidence**.

| Tier | Lives in | Promises | Requires |
|---|---|---|---|
| Proposal | `proposals/<name>/` | nothing | a scope doc and a working prototype |
| Canon | `tokens/` + `src/` | a versioned contract | every gate below green |

A proposal exists so an unstable idea can be examined without the package
claiming to ship it. A proposal can move three rules in a single day of drawing
posters. Canon has stopped moving.

**Promotion is the commit.** "Adding something to Konstrukt" means moving it
from the left column to the right one, in one pull request, with this checklist
complete. The text layer is the worked example: it lived under
`proposals/text-layer/` and shipped in 1.2.0 as `tokens/text.json` plus
`src/text/` and a build output.

## Promotion checklist

Nothing enters canon until all seven are true. The order matters: the gate
before the docs, the docs before the release.

1. **Token.** The new values live in `tokens/*.json` as W3C DTCG, not as
   literals in a consumer, not as a constant in a script. Glyphs, ladders,
   column budgets and scale ranges are design decisions and therefore tokens.
2. **Build output.** `npm run build` emits it, so every language gets it from
   source. Consumers never read `tokens/` directly.
3. **Gate.** A check that fails the build when the contract breaks:
   `npm run check` for token parity and WCAG contrast, `npm run check:text` for the text-layer
   linter and a golden board render. **A new output without a gate is a
   new source of drift.**
4. **Lint.** Rules that can be mechanised are mechanised. A documented rule with
   no check is a preference, and preferences rot.
5. **Docs.** A page under `docs/` in the `components.html` anatomy: one section
   per primitive, a demo rendered from the built output, a copy-ready
   snippet, and the rule stated as a rule. Register it in the nav.
6. **Consumer.** One real surface uses it in the same PR, and the PR body shows
   the before and after. **A primitive is not real until a surface consumes it.**
   This is the step people skip, and it is the only one that proves the contract
   is usable rather than merely describable.
7. **Release.** `CHANGELOG.md` entry, semver bump, tag. Consumers pin the tag.

## Version policy

Semver applies to the **token contract**, not to the repo's activity.

- **minor**: new tokens, new primitives, new output target. The text layer
  landing in 1.2.0 is the example.
- **patch**: generated-output fixes that do not change a token name or value.
- **major**: renaming or removing a token, changing a ladder's meaning, changing
  what a status word means. Anything that makes a consumer's render wrong
  without an error.

## Propagation

Consumers fall into three kinds, and each has one correct mechanism.

1. **Built from source** (site, pages): import the generated CSS at the pinned
   version. No copying.
2. **Vendored by copy** (standalone scripts, cron collectors, anything that
   cannot take an npm dependency): copy the generated file, and stamp the copy:
   ```python
   # konstrukt-text v1.2.0  sha256:3f9c…  do not edit
   ```
   A copy without a version stamp is indistinguishable from a fork.
3. **Hand-declared** (a token block pasted into a page's own stylesheet):
   tolerated only for throwaway artifacts, and registered in `consumers.json` so
   `npm run verify` can diff it against `dist` and report the first differing
   line. If it matters, it is kind 1.

## What never goes in canon

- A primitive with no consumer.
- A glyph ladder that exists only inside one script.
- A rule whose only enforcement is a sentence in a prompt.
- Anything whose spec lives in a slide, a Paper document or a chat message. The
  repo is the version of the truth; everything else is a derivative that must be
  regenerated from it.
